title: Release metadata
description:
What the repository says about one release: its hash and the organization that owns its name (publisher-trust spec §5.1, §6.2). Signed by the repository ROOT key, in the same envelope as the organization key document.

SERVED AS `signed` INSIDE THE /v2/resolve BODY, beside the plain v2 fields. The signed half is authoritative and the plain half is never merged into it: one response then serves both a verifying and a non-verifying client, and a mirror that rewrites the plain half accomplishes nothing. A bare envelope is also accepted, which is the shape the filesystem driver reads from a `<name>-<version>.release.json` sidecar.

THE PAYLOAD IS CARRIED AS OPAQUE BYTES ON PURPOSE, exactly as in org-key-document.json: the signature covers the decoded `payload` as transmitted, so there is no canonical-JSON step for signer and verifier to disagree about.

format.description: Envelope version. A client that does not recognise the value refuses the document rather than guessing at its meaning.

root-key-id.description: Which root key signed this. A hint for picking a candidate when a client holds several; the client reports the root that actually verified, not this claim (spec §6.3).

payload.description: base64 of the UTF-8 JSON described by $defs/release.

signature.description: base64 ed25519 signature over the DECODED payload bytes.

name.description: The archive's dotted name. Strongly recommended: it makes the signed statement self-identifying, so a client that checks it cannot be made to accept this statement under another coordinate.

version.description: The archive's version. Recommended for the same reason as `name`.

sha256.description: The archive's content hash, `sha256:<hex>` or bare hex (the client normalises to the prefixed form). This is the hash fetched bytes are checked against — the unsigned `.sha256` sidecar beside it is ignored when this is present (spec §5.1).

organization.description: The organization that owns this name. This is what binds the archive to a publisher, and it is the reason verification costs no extra round trip: the resolve the client already performs answers 'who owns this'. It MUST come from the authority that gated the upload and MUST NOT be computed from the name (spec §4.4).
